summary.text: A 70-year-old former heavy smoker was diagnosed with extensive disease small-cell lung cancer of the left lung in June 2019 and presented with jaundice, hepatomegaly and liver failure from massive liver dissemination, with lymph node involvement and ECOG PS 1.
Laboratory tests showed a G4 bilirubin increase (14.81 mg/dl), G3 AST elevation (303 U/L) and serum creatinine 1.8 mg/dl; Table 1 lists further values before the first carboplatin cycle.

First-line single-agent carboplatin (AUC 3.5, total dose 300 mg) was started with GFR 61.76 ml/min. Laboratory tests improved until normalization, documenting complete recovery of liver function; four cycles were given at increasing doses (maximum AUC 4.5), with a partial response of primary tumor and liver metastases on post-treatment CT.

After four cycles bone marrow failure developed, needing G-CSF and blood transfusion support and precluding further treatment; bone marrow biopsy showed severe hypocellularity suggestive of myelofibrosis. The patient died 150 days from the start of treatment.
